summary: Completed the bounded F65 Phase 1 frontend: an N-row, actor-scoped, durable paged group review alongside the unchanged legacy pair merge. It shows original member catalog, stock and lot provenance beside server-computed resolved economics and projections, retains explicit source choices across pages, reports canonical progress, and keeps Apply and independent Remove unavailable.
changes: Added the exact resolution-v2 preview request/response types and read-only POST/GET transport without offline write replay.
Added N-row request construction, stable member ordering, explicit source-choice validation, blank-value preservation, and canonical paged-progress helpers.
Added a separate global group-review action and modal while preserving the existing exact-pair preview/apply flow.
Rendered every member's catalog identity, prices, branch stock, lot/batch identity, supplier, received/expiry dates, received quantity/cost, payment/due status, and active state.
Rendered server-computed distinct-nonzero mean cost, maximum prices, projected branch stock, lot count and projected quantity; added explicit keeper and barcode/category/brand/unit source selectors.
Added bilingual Phase 1 wording, disabled Apply and Remove affordances, and kept non-destructive Dismiss visibly distinct from Remove.
Added focused contract, paging, transport-boundary, source-choice, component, and legacy coexistence assertions.

risks: The Phase 1 choices are retained while the modal is open and guarded against accidental close, but are not finalized or persisted as resolution choices because the Phase 2 finalize contract is intentionally outside this slice.

The repository's standard local migration wrapper batched pending migrations into a SQLite compound-term limit during the independent browser setup; the browser tester applied the same local migrations one transaction at a time. This did not affect the production source or remote data.
